newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran president meets Iraqi president envoy.
newsitem.headline: Iran president meets Iraqi president envoy.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani met an envoy of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein amid mounting tension over charges of Iranian intervention in northern Iraq, the official news agency IRNA said on Wednesday.
It said Rafsanjani received on Tuesday the unnamed envoy who delivered a message to him from Saddam Hussein.

"The Iraqi envoy voiced Iraq's desire for good neighbourly relations with Iran and for expansion of mutual relations. He also called for cooperation and exchange of views between the two countries on regional issues," IRNA said.
"President Rafsanjani underlined the need for making efforts to solve the issue of war prisoners and to completely enforce all articles of the U.N. Resolution 598," the agency said.

The United Nations resolution led to a ceasefire which ended the 1980-88 war. Accounting for war prisoners is among the thorniest issues hindering efforts to improve ties between Tehran and Baghdad. Iran also says Iraq should pay hundreds of billions of dollars in war damages.
Rafsanjani "also underscored the importance of good neighbourly relations between the two countries," IRNA added.
The visit, a rare event in the relation between the former war foes, came amid repeated Iraqi accusation of Iranian interference in Iraq's northern Kurdish areas.

In Baghdad, Iraqi Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi on Wednesday accused Iran of meddling in northern Iraq and urged Tehran to steer away from fighting between rival Kurdish factions.

Iran has denied earlier charges by Massoud Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), that Iranian forces entered northern Iraq to help rival guerrillas of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) retake a key city on Sunday.
Baghdad has said its intrusion in Kurdish northern Iraq in late August, which helped the KDP capture the Kurdish capital Arbil, was aimed at backing the KDP against the PUK and Iran.
